podcast.body: The Village People initially objected to Donald Trump's campaign using "YMCA" at rallies. This objection was part of a larger trend where numerous artists tried to prevent their music from being associated with political campaigns, often through cease and desist orders and lawsuits. "even the village people initially wanted Trump to stop using YMCA and Macho Man at Israelis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

podcast.body: This song, featuring a group of guys in costumes (one dressed in leather) singing about cruising other guys at the YMCA, achieved widespread popularity, being played in roller rinks, ballparks, and weddings. Its mainstream acceptance is attributed to its theatrical and performance-oriented nature, which allowed audiences to enjoy it without confronting its underlying gay themes as "real." "singing about cruising other guys at the YMCA, and America loves this?"
